newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian farmers destroy bananas in Jericho.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian farmers destroy bananas in Jericho.

text.p: Palestinian farmers in the West Bank town of Jericho on Monday destroyed tonnes of bananas on Monday to protest against restrictions on agricultural exports
Witnesses said angry farmers threw their bananas from trucks and drove over them, smashing produce they are barred from exporting to traditional markets in Israel and Jordan.
"Because there is a closure and we can't sell our bananas in Israeli or Jordanian markets, we have an oversupply," banana grower Mazen Barakat told Reuters.

Israel has periodically imposed closures barring Palestinian goods and workers from the Jewish state since 1994, the year Jericho was handed over to Palestinian self-rule under landmark Israeli-PLO peace deals.
Barakat said Jordan imposed restrictions on Palestinian produce soon after Jericho fell under Palestinian rule, cutting off markets for some 1,000 tonnes of monthly banana exports.
He said annual Palestinian banana production stood at around 25,000 tonnes.
Farmers said while their bananas rotted in self-ruled Jericho, Israeli bananas were flooding Palestinian markets.
"Halt the Israeli banana invasion of Palestinian markets!" said one banner carried by farmers demonstrating in the centre of usually sleepy Jericho.
"While we can't export, Israelis export to us around 60,000 tonnes annually," Barakat said.
Palestinian Agriculture Minister Abdel-Jawad Saleh said closures violated a 1994 Israeli-PLO economic protocol guaranteeing Palestinian access to Israeli markets.
"Israel is violating all international agreements and resolutions and it is high time to treat Israel in the same way it treats Palestinians," Saleh said.
"This should be done by closing Palestinian markets to Israeli produce," Saleh told the farmers.
Palestinians consider Israeli closures collective punishment. Closures have devastated the already struggling Palestinian economy.
